title: QBR Billing & Usage Playbook — Spend, Rate Limits, Alerts
content:
Purpose:
This is a working QBR worksheet + playbook focused on billing and usage signals customers care about: token spend trends, rate limit incidents, budget alerts, and renewal/commit guidance. Use as a live doc during customer prep and the QBR meeting.

How to use: 
- Fill the Metrics section with the latest 90-day window.
- Attach relevant billing exports (CSV) and ticket links.
- Convert Action items into Jira tickets (label: cs-qbr).

---
1) Executive TL;DR (1–2 lines)
- Last quarter spend trend: e.g., "Up 35% QoQ driven by embed-heavy feature; cost/1k tokens increased due to model upgrade"
- Any material rate-limit or throttling incidents impacting SLAs: yes/no + short note
- Recommendation headline for renewal: increase committed units / keep PAYG + introduce budget alerts

2) Key metrics (populate with exact numbers) — default window: 90 days
- Total tokens (input): ____________
- Billable tokens (input): ____________
- Avg cost per 1k tokens (customer effective): ____________
- Spend by product area (approx): generation: $__, embeddings: $__, rerank: $__
- Peak sustained TPS (tokens/sec): ____________
- 95th/99th pct latency for top route: 95p=__, 99p=__
- Monthly active API keys: ____, Top 3 API keys by spend: (name/id + % of spend)

3) Rate limit & throttle review
- Total 429 events (90d): ____
- Unique customers/teams impacted: ____
- Most common route(s) throttled: e.g., /v1/generate-chat, /v1/embeddings
- Root causes (check all that apply): sudden traffic spike; mis-configured retry; no client-side backoff; intentional scraping; batch mis-sizing; other: ____
- Customer self-remediation notes: client retries fixed? SDK updated?

4) Budget alerts & quota configuration summary
- Current customer alert thresholds (if any): daily spend alert: $__, monthly cap: $__
- Recommended alerts to add before renewal: 3 tiers (informational @50%, warning @75%, hard cap @95%)
- Suggested automated actions on hitting tiers: notify billing owner; open incident; throttle non-critical routes; auto-scale fallback to cheaper model variant
- TODO: confirm which email/slack channels the alerts route to (Ops, Eng, Product)

5) Recommendations (operational + contractual)
- Short term (next 30 days): set alert tiers, add token-level dashboards, enable prefix caching for generation where applicable
- Medium term (30–90 days): introduce request-level sampling to reduce expensive preview calls, review caching strategies for embeddings, implement client backoff/retry best-practices
- Contractual: evaluate a small reserved commit for peak season (X% discount) vs PAYG with stronger alerting; propose a 6-month pilot commit if repeat overrun observed

6) Playbook: incident checklist for billing/rate-limit spikes (use during on-call and CS escalations)
- Step 0: Triage — pull billing ledger (last 7 days) + top API key usage, identify spike start time
- Step 1: Isolate route(s) — identify endpoints and models involved
- Step 2: Short-term mitigation — set temporary per-key rate limits, suggest downgraded model variant or enforced sampling
- Step 3: Customer comms — draft message template below, include ETA and mitigation steps
- Step 4: Longer-term fix — open engineering ticket to add caching, batching, or model reroute
- Escalation: If 429s > 1% of requests or spend > 130% forecasted monthly budget, escalate to CS manager + SRE on-call

7) QBR talking points & suggested slide bullets
- "Last 90 days we saw X tokens (+Y% QoQ). Most spend driven by Z feature; suggested optimization: [cache + batch]."
- "We observed N throttles on [route]. Short-term mitigation applied; engineering ticket #_____ opened for root cause."
- "We propose a tailored commit that reduces unit cost by P% and buys predictability during your expected growth window."
- Include 2–3 action items with owners and dates (see Action items table)

8) Customer comms templates (short)
- Incident notification (to customer): 
  Hi <Name>,
  We detected increased usage on <route> starting <time>. We have applied temporary safeguards and are investigating the root cause. Expected next update in 2 hours. Suggested immediate step: enable client-side backoff and avoid full-batch embedding refreshes until issue resolved.

- Renewal suggestion snippet:
  Recommended commit: $<amount>/mo for 6 months to cover forecasted peak and get unit discount of ~X%. Add automated alerts at 50/75/95% to prevent surprises.

9) Action items table (to be converted into tickets)
- [ ] Create token spend dashboard for top 5 keys (owner: Maya — due: 2025-02-20)
- [ ] Configure 3-tier budget alerts for production org (owner: Priya — due: 2025-02-15)
- [ ] Open engineering ticket for route-level throttling investigation (owner: Diego — JIRA-7890)

10) Data extraction snippets (notes for SRE/eng)
- Billing export columns to request: date, api_key, model, tokens, billable_tokens, cost_usd, route
- Suggested quick SQL: 
  SELECT api_key, SUM(tokens) AS tokens, SUM(cost_usd) AS spend
  FROM billing.events
  WHERE ts BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-03-01'
  GROUP BY api_key ORDER BY spend DESC LIMIT 20;
- Note: confirm if "billable_tokens" already includes embedding multipliers for this customer region

11) Open questions / notes to self (working)
- Does this customer have private deployment discounts applied separately? check contract clause 4.2
- Are we double-counting cached prefix tokens in billing export? flag to finance
- Can we propose a small pilot commit with auto-scaling burst to avoid throttles during forecasted events?

Attachments to add before QBR:
- Last 3 months billing CSV (exported)
- Top-20 API key sample (CSV)
- Incident timeline (if any) with 429 counts by hour
- Draft renewal quote (if proposing commit)

Draft status notes: informal checklist above — this is intentionally lightweight. Convert to a formal QBR slide if customer wants an executive summary.

----
End of worksheet.

Notes: keep a copy in the customer folder under /shared_drives/customer-success/<customer-name>/qbrs and attach the final slides and the ticket list.
